title: Contributing to Isoformic
text: Fork package clone onto computer. haven’t done , recommend using usethis::create_from_github("luciorq/isoformic", fork = TRUE). Install development dependencies devtools::install_dev_deps(), make sure package passes R CMD check running devtools::check(). R CMD check doesn’t pass cleanly, ’s good idea ask help continuing. Create Git branch pull request (PR). recommend using usethis::pr_init("brief-description--change"). Make changes, commit git, create PR running usethis::pr_push(), following prompts browser. title PR briefly describe change. body PR contain Fixes #issue-number. user-facing changes, add bullet top NEWS.md (.e. just first header). title: Case study: a splicing kinase inhibitor in nanopore long reads
text: CLK genes among : lorecivivint raises one protein coding isoform CLK1, CLK3 CLK4.  gene-level results show classification needs care. CLK1 CLK3 significant DESeq2, shrunken fold changes (1.8-fold) cutoff 2-fold, isoform_switches() count changed genes: isoforms CLK1 explain gene-level change. CLK1-201 encodes full-length kinase; CLK1-204 transcript without exon 4, shifts reading frame makes target nonsense-mediated decay; CLK1-210 keeps introns sides exon 4. CLK1 activity favours skipping exon 4, CLK inhibitors shift balance towards full-length isoform (Uzor et al. 2018). long reads show shift: full-length isoform rises 17 46 transcripts per million skipped one falls 4 1.5 (significant , q = 0.25).
code: plot_log2fc(iso, feature = c("CLK1", "CLK3", "CLK4"), ncol = 2) deg |>   left_join(annot_data_genes(iso)[c("gene_id", "gene_name")], by = "gene_id") |>   filter(gene_name %in% c("CLK1", "CLK3", "CLK4")) |>   select(gene_name, log2FC, qvalue, deg_sig) #> # A tibble: 3 × 4 #>   gene_name log2FC      qvalue deg_sig #>   <chr>      <dbl>       <dbl> <chr>   #> 1 CLK1       0.873 0.000000274 no      #> 2 CLK3       0.858 0.0000568   no      #> 3 CLK4       0.707 0.0598      no plot_tx_expr(iso, gene_name = "CLK1", group = "condition") plot_genomic_context(iso, gene_name = "CLK1")

title: Transcriptomic diversity
text: tx_diversity() summarises gene uses isoforms: many annotated, assayed expressed, many transcript types span, isoform dominates effective number isoforms (1 single isoform carries expression, equal number isoforms expressed evenly).

title: Functional enrichment by transcript type
text: run_enrichment() expands gene sets transcripts genes runs gene set enrichment analysis (fgsea) separately protein coding transcripts unproductive categories (retained intron, nonsense-mediated decay transcripts without defined coding sequence), combined individually. result can stored object saved . plot_enrichment() draws pathways side side transcript category.

title: Introduction to isoformic
text: isoformic interprets RNA-seq data level annotated transcripts. Instead asking whether gene changes conditions, asks isoforms change, type transcript (protein coding, retained intron, nonsense-mediated decay, …) expression gene distributed across . Everything revolves around IsoformicExperiment object. holds, samples, transcript-level assays, gene-level assays derived , exon structures every annotated transcript differential expression results, backed Parquet files disk. article builds object quantification differential expression tables shows look . analyses one article : Transcriptomic diversity: many isoforms gene uses, one dominates isoform switches happen. Quantification uncertainty: well reads determine isoform, isoforms told apart confident differential expression call . makes isoform hard quantify?: isoforms reads leave uncertain, , many Gibbs draws enough. Isoform structure productivity: open reading frames, nonsense-mediated decay, productive fractions, poison exons external evidence. Alternative polyadenylation: 3’ end usage 3’ UTR length. Functional enrichment transcript type: gene set enrichment run separately coding unproductive transcripts. Plots: fold-change, expression profile genomic context plots. annotations: T2T-CHM13, Ensembl, RefSeq, haplotype-resolved assemblies, FANTOM CAT long-read catalogs. Working plain tables: table-based counterparts every step. start Salmon output instead ready-made tables, see Salmon quantifications IsoformicExperiment. examples use placenta RNA-seq dataset “Landscape Dysregulated Placental RNA Editing Associated Preeclampsia”: 8 preeclamptic 17 control placentas quantified Salmon (Patro et al. 2017) GENCODE v33 tested differential expression transcript level swish (Zhu et al. 2019) gene level DESeq2. tables ship package Parquet files. isoformic relies transcript types GENCODE annotation. annotation must one used quantification, GENCODE v33. download_reference() fetches package cache (step needs internet connection first time) prepare_isoformic_annotation() converts GFF3 file, , directory Parquet tables. tables can inspected read_parquet(), normally object reads . cache location every setting package reads documented ?isoformic-options. transcript-level abundance table (TPM) sample metadata needed. Transcript IDs checked annotation, sample IDs metadata. object behaves like SummarizedExperiment: Gene-level assays derived demand summing isoforms gene cached. Results tool can attached: column names log2FoldChange, padj, logFC FDR standardised log2FC, pvalue qvalue, IDs validated annotation. Significance flagged stored cutoffs (absolute log2 fold-change 1 adjusted p-value 0.05 default). de_table() combines levels one long table, one row per feature, plots consume. fold-change plot compares change gene transcripts, coloured transcript type; plots article covers others.  whole object, including results, written directory Parquet files restored read_isoformic(). title: From Salmon quantifications to an IsoformicExperiment
text: recommend Salmon (Patro et al. 2017) selective-alignment mode GENCODE transcriptome, inferential replicates swish (Zhu et al. 2019) can used transcript-level differential expression. Salmon 2 -scratch rewrite Rust (2.8.0 time writing). workflow (salmon index, salmon quant, quant.sf) output files , read_salmon(), tximeta, tximport swish work unchanged, index format new: index built Salmon 1.x rejected must rebuilt (last C++ release, 1.12.0, remains available salmon-cpp conda package). changes worth knowing: selective alignment mapping mode (--validateMappings -op), quantification deterministic default (identical output thread count), decoy sequences longer appear quant.sf, --ignoreTxVersion matches transcript identifiers without version suffix gene map given. Salmon migration guide lists every removed ignored option. typical single-sample invocation shell : --libType detects library type, index built GENCODE transcript FASTA salmon index --gencode (truncates transcript names first |), --posBias --seqBias --gcBias correct biases, --dumpEq --dumpEqWeights keep equivalence classes --numGibbsSamples writes inferential replicates swish needs aux_info/bootstrap/. can driven R condathis package, installs Salmon Bioconda conda environment (Linux macOS, WSL2 Windows). salmon_index() salmon_quant() run commands ; first call creates environment Salmon 2.8.0: salmon_quant() draws 30 Gibbs samples per sample default (num_gibbs = 0 skips ). Besides swish, quantify well reads determine isoform, isoforms told apart confident differential expression call ; read_salmon(inferential = TRUE) reads uncertainty article explains use report . decoy-aware index (recommended Salmon authors), build gentrome FASTA decoys.txt genome described Salmon documentation pass --decoys decoys.txt salmon index.
code: salmon index \   --transcripts gencode.v49.transcripts.fa.gz \   --index salmon_index \   --gencode \   --threads 8  salmon quant \   --libType A \   --index salmon_index \   --mates1 /path/SRR..._1.fastq.gz \   --mates2 /path/SRR..._2.fastq.gz \   --output /path/SRR..._quant \   --threads 8 \   --allowDovetail --softclipOverhangs \   --dumpEq --dumpEqWeights \   --posBias --seqBias --gcBias \   --numGibbsSamples 30 library(isoformic) tx_fasta <- download_reference(version = "49", file_type = "fasta") gff_path <- download_reference(version = "49", file_type = "gff")  salmon_index(fasta_path = tx_fasta, index_path = "salmon_index", is_gencode = TRUE, num_threads = 8) salmon_quant(   input_r1 = "sample_1.fastq.gz",   input_r2 = "sample_2.fastq.gz",   index_path = "salmon_index",   output_dir = "quants/sample_quant",   num_threads = 8 )

title: From Salmon quantifications to an IsoformicExperiment

text: as_summarized_experiment() exports gene-level assays (isoforms summed, lengths averaged abundance) DESeq2 can run .
code: se_gene <- as_summarized_experiment(iso, level = "gene") assay(se_gene, "counts") <- round(assay(se_gene, "counts")) se_gene$condition <- factor(se_gene$condition, levels = c("control", "treatment"))  dds <- DESeq2::DESeqDataSet(se_gene, design = ~condition) dds <- dds[rowSums(DESeq2::counts(dds) >= 10) >= 3, ] dds <- DESeq2::DESeq(dds, quiet = TRUE) res <- DESeq2::results(dds, contrast = c("condition", "treatment", "control")) shrink_type <- if (rlang::is_installed("apeglm")) "apeglm" else "normal" res_shr <- DESeq2::lfcShrink(dds, coef = "condition_treatment_vs_control", res = res, type = shrink_type, quiet = TRUE)  de_gene(iso) <- as.data.frame(res_shr) head(de_gene(iso)) #> # A tibble: 6 × 7 #>   gene_id            baseMean       log2FC   lfcSE   pvalue  qvalue deg_sig #>   <chr>                 <dbl>        <dbl>   <dbl>    <dbl>   <dbl> <chr>   #> 1 ENSG00000125538.12    140.   3.94        1.55    0.000218 0.00196 yes     #> 2 ENSG00000115415.22    435.   0.00000191  0.00144 0.452    0.614   no      #> 3 ENSG00000100906.13   1212.  -0.00000132  0.00144 0.362    0.614   no      #> 4 ENSG00000271503.7   20364.  -0.000000869 0.00144 0.477    0.614   no      #> 5 ENSG00000184557.5     241.   0.000000810 0.00144 0.586    0.659   no      #> 6 ENSG00000073756.13     63.9  0.000000600 0.00144 0.438    0.614   no iso #> <IsoformicExperiment> mini_placenta #>   annotation : gencode_v49_mini_subset (15 genes, 111 transcripts, 1,071 exons) #>   samples    : 6 [condition] #>   transcripts: 111 assayed from 15 genes #>   assays     : abundance, counts, length #>   gene assays: derived from transcript assays on demand #>   DE results : det (111 transcripts), deg (12 genes)

title: Isoform structure and productivity
text: transcript_productivity() turns features graded call, reason: productive: complete ORF identical canonical one; altered_productive: complete ORF, NMD, different protein; unproductive: ORF, NMD predicted unproductive biotype; noncoding; uncertain: enough information (example incomplete CDS annotation). productive_fraction() share gene’s expression carried productive isoforms, per condition, change. gene whose total expression flat productive fraction falls regulated post-transcriptionally.

Methods. uncertainty_methods() writes paragraph Salmon version, number draws cutoffs; edit fit. cautions belong text well. draws describe uncertainty quantification ; replace biological replicates, isoform stable fold-change can still false positive primary test. cutoffs (inf_rv_cutoff, cor_cutoff, min_agreement) heuristics: rerun add_uncertainty() values report numbers change. classes calibrated nothing data hand. code: report <- uncertainty_report(iso) names(report) #> [1] "settings"    "run"         "transcripts" "genes"       "de"          #> [6] "switches" report$transcripts #> # A tibble: 4 × 7 #>   transcript_type n_assessed n_uncertain pct_uncertain median_inf_rv n_ambiguous #>   <chr>                <int>       <int>         <dbl>         <dbl>       <int> #> 1 protein_coding         364         333          91.5         7.47           25 #> 2 retained_intron         75          41          54.7         0.589           1 #> 3 protein_coding…         25          21          84           1.32            0 #> 4 nonsense_media…         17          16          94.1         4.76            0 #> # ℹ 1 more variable: median_unique_fraction <dbl> report$de #> # A tibble: 3 × 5 #>   confidence n_significant n_unstable n_uncertain n_ambiguous #>   <ord>              <int>      <int>       <int>       <int> #> 1 high                   3          0           0           0 #> 2 moderate              20          0          20           0 #> 3 low                    5          0           5           5 report$switches #> NULL uncertainty_methods(iso) #> [1] "Transcript abundances were quantified with Salmon 2.8.0 and 30 Gibbs samples per sample were used to measure the inferential uncertainty of each isoform. For every transcript, the inferential relative variance (InfRV; Zhu et al. 2019) was averaged over samples, and transcripts with an InfRV of at least 0.5 were called uncertain. The correlation between the replicates of isoforms of the same gene was averaged over samples, and isoform pairs with a correlation of -0.5 or lower were called ambiguous and grouped. The log2 fold-change of each isoform was recomputed on every replicate (counts scaled to a common library size, pseudocount 5), and a fold-change was called stable when at least 95% of the replicates agreed on its direction. Differentially expressed isoforms were assigned high confidence when the fold-change was stable, the quantification was not uncertain and no sibling isoform was ambiguous, moderate confidence when one of these conditions failed and low confidence when two or more failed. Only transcripts with a mean estimated count of at least 1 were assessed. The contrast was knockdown versus control in the condition variable."

Three levels, one object assay(iso, "abundance")[1:3, 1:3]   # transcripts x samples gene_assay(iso, "abundance")[1:3, 1:3] # genes x samples, summed from isoforms head(exon_table(iso, "RBPJ"))        # exon structures from the annotation  # Transcriptomic diversity head(tx_diversity(iso))               # expressed isoforms, dominant isoform, effective number head(transcript_features(iso))        # ORF, UTRs, NMD rule, promoters, splicing events vs canonical head(transcript_productivity(iso))    # productive / altered / unproductive / noncoding, with reasons head(productive_fraction(iso, group = "condition")) # productive share of each gene and its change dominant_isoform(iso, group = "condition") # dominance switches between groups isoform_switches(iso)                 # transcript vs gene level differential expression  # Plots plot_log2fc(iso, feature = "RBPJ") plot_tx_expr(iso, gene_name = "RBPJ", group = "condition") plot_genomic_context(iso, gene_name = "RBPJ") annot <- prepare_isoformic_annotation("gencode.v49.annotation.gff3.gz") # title: Accessors for IsoformicExperiment Objects — IsoformicExperiment-accessors
text: S7 generics giving SummarizedExperiment-style access three levels IsoformicExperiment. return -memory tibbles matrices; annotation tables read Parquet first use cached (see class documentation). Samples col_data(), col_data<-: sample metadata (sample_id first). col_names(): sample IDs assays. Transcript level assays(), assay(x, name), assay_names(), assay<-: transcript matrices. assay() without name returns first assay. row_names(): transcript IDs assays. row_data(): transcript annotation (gene columns) assayed transcripts, assay row order. tx_annot(): join annotated transcripts. tx_to_gene(): two-column transcript/gene mapping. Gene level gene_assays(), gene_assay(x, name), gene_assays<-: gene matrices, derived summing isoforms unless set explicitly. gene_data(): gene annotation genes represented assays. gene_names(): gene IDs gene assays. Annotation annot_data_transcripts(), annot_data_genes(), annot_data_exons(): raw annotation tables. annot_data(): transcript-centric join transcripts genes (exons optional). annot_metadata(): named list describing annotation source. exon_table(x, gene_name): exons transcripts selected genes. Housekeeping clear_cache(): drop cached derived data object (, annotation = TRUE, shared annotation tables).

what: IsoformicExperiment: Transcript, Gene and Exon Level Data in One Object — IsoformicExperiment
title: IsoformicExperiment: Transcript, Gene and Exon Level Data in One Object — IsoformicExperiment
text: IsoformicExperiment S7 class modelled SummarizedExperiment, organised around transcriptomic diversity: samples described three levels kept consistent construction. Transcript level: assays numeric matrices transcript IDs row names sample IDs column names (example abundance, counts, length). assays share dimnames. Gene level: gene assays derived transcript assays summing isoforms gene (abundance-weighted means length), cached, can overridden gene_assays<-. Exon level: exon structures come annotation available annot_data_exons(), exon_table() exon_diversity(). Annotation never copied object. annot_path property points annotation directory Parquet files created prepare_isoformic_annotation() (GFF3/GTF file accepted converted fly). Tables read DuckDB first access cached memory keyed file path, size modification time, re-created annotation picked automatically several objects sharing one annotation share one copy tables. Derived results (gene assays, row data, isoform fractions) cached per object .cache environment, keyed hash inputs, therefore survive copies never go stale. See clear_cache(). Objects persist disk directory Parquet files write_isoformic() restored read_isoformic().

what: Build the Frozen Datasets from Their Sources — build_frozen_data
title: Build the Frozen Datasets from Their Sources — build_frozen_data
text: function downloads source files one frozen dataset (see frozen_datasets()) sources cache, converts Parquet table used package returns file path. fetch_frozen_data() runs frozen file downloaded, data-raw/build_frozen_data.R runs publish new version. resulting tables: build_frozen_appris(): one row per transcript appris_annotation (PRINCIPAL:1 ALTERNATIVE:2, MINOR), appris_score, method scores (firestar_residues, matador_structure, corsair_conservation, spade_domain_score, thump_tm_helices, crash_signal, trifid_score), protein_length, ccds_id mane label. build_frozen_appris_domains(): one row per Pfam domain per transcript genomic span (seqid, start_pos, end_pos, strand), pfam_acc, pfam_name, evalue, pep_start, pep_end. build_frozen_riboseq_orfs(): one row per Ribo-seq ORF phase, genomic span, block_starts/block_ends (1-based, ;-separated), orf_type, gene_id, gene_name, transcript_ids (compatible transcripts, phase 1 ), replicated studies. build_frozen_nmd_exons(): one row per validated NMD-inducing exon seqid, start_pos, end_pos, strand, flanking exons, nmd_transcript_ids, non_nmd_transcript_ids, gene_id, gene_name. Reading supplementary spreadsheet needs readxl package. build_frozen_polyasite(): one row per poly() site cluster seqid, start_pos, end_pos, cleavage_pos, strand, tpm, frac_samples, n_protocols, site_class (TE terminal exon, EX exon, intron, DS downstream, AE/AI/AU antisense, IG intergenic) signals. build_frozen_gtex(): one row per transcript tissue median_tpm n_samples (GTEx v8, RSEM transcript TPM; identifiers GENCODE v26, stored without version).

what: Differential Expression Results in an IsoformicExperiment — dea
title: Differential Expression Results in an IsoformicExperiment — dea
text: IsoformicExperiment stores differential expression results transcripts (det) genes (deg) dea property, together significance cutoffs used flag features. Results can come tool: assignment tables standardised column names log2FC, pvalue qvalue (see Details), checked annotation, stored tibbles. de_tx(x) / de_gene(x): results added det_sig / deg_sig column ("yes"/"") computed cutoffs, sorted absolute log2FC. Cutoffs can overridden per call. de_tx(x) <- value / de_gene(x) <- value: set results. de_cutoffs(x) / de_cutoffs(x) <- value: stored cutoffs, list log2fc (default 1), pvalue (default 0.05) use_fdr (default TRUE, .e. compare qvalue rather pvalue). de_table(x): long table combining gene transcript results, one row per feature, feature_id, feature_name, feature_type ("gene" transcript type), gene_id, gene_name, log2FC, pvalue, qvalue is_de. input plot_log2fc().

title: Transcriptomic Diversity Summaries — diversity
text: generics quantify expression distributed across isoforms gene, question IsoformicExperiment built answer. computations use matrix operations cached assays scale full transcriptome experiments. isoform_fraction(x): matrix (transcripts x samples) fraction gene's expression carried transcript. NA gene expressed sample. tx_diversity(x): one row per gene summarising isoform usage: number annotated, assayed expressed isoforms, number transcript types, dominant isoform mean fraction, effective number isoforms (exp(Shannon entropy) mean isoform fractions, 1 = single isoform carries expression). dominant_isoform(x, group): dominant isoform gene, overall per level col_data column, flagging genes whose dominant isoform changes groups (dominant_switch). isoform_switches(x): relates transcript- gene-level differential expression per gene: counts significant isoforms , gene-level call switch_type classification ("opposite_direction", "det_not_deg", "consistent"). exon_diversity(x, gene_name): per gene, number distinct exons, many constitutive (shared isoforms) versus alternative, mean number exons per isoform. haplotype_summary(x, group): haplotype-resolved annotations (see merge_annotations()), expression gene per haplotype, haplotype fraction (allelic imbalance), dominant isoform haplotype (compared source_transcript_id) whether dominant isoform differs haplotypes (haplotype_isoform_switch). Genes matched across haplotypes source_gene_id, falling back gene_name. dominant_isoform() also reports dominant_is_canonical, whether dominant isoform MANE Select / Ensembl canonical / RefSeq Select transcript gene. object carries uncertainty tables (see add_uncertainty()) adds dominant_inf_rv, inferential relative variance dominant isoform, dominant_ambiguous, whether told apart sibling isoform. isoform_switches() adds n_det_confident, number significant isoforms high confidence, de_confidence() results stored.

what: Download Reference Annotations and Sequences — download_reference
title: Download Reference Annotations and Sequences — download_reference
text: Downloads annotation (GFF3/GTF) sequence (transcript genome FASTA) files main public providers: "gencode" (default): GENCODE release human (GRCh38) mouse (GRCm39), including future releases. "ensembl": Ensembl release, species division (vertebrates, plants, metazoa, fungi, protists). "ncbi": NCBI assembly accession (example GCF_009914755.1 T2T-CHM13v2.0, GCF_000001405.40 GRCh38.p14). "t2t": shorthand reference = "ncbi", accession = "GCF_009914755.1" (telomere--telomere T2T-CHM13v2.0). "mane": MANE (Matched Annotation NCBI EMBL-EBI) releases, canonical transcript per protein-coding gene, Ensembl RefSeq coordinates identifiers. "fantom": FANTOM CAT transcriptome assembly (Hon et al. 2017; GRCh37/hg19) one levels (version = "lv3_robust" default; "lv1_raw", "lv2_permissive", "lv4_stringent"), GTF . FANTOM6 analyses use lv3 robust catalog. companion ID mapping, gene information CAGE cluster tables come download_fantom_cat_tables(). Instead assuming file names, function lists release directory server picks matching file, new releases new genome patch versions (example GRCh38.p15) work without package update. Files already present output_path downloaded . file reachable URL (example T2T consortium Liftoff GFF3 files) can cached way download_reference_url(), HPRC per-haplotype annotations download_hprc_annotation().

title: Download Reference Annotations and Sequences — download_reference
text: version Release version. GENCODE: release number ("49", 49, "M38" / "38" mouse; default "49"). Ensembl: release number ("116"); NULL (default) uses current release. MANE: "1.5"; NULL uses current release. NCBI/T2T: ignored (accession identifies assembly version). reference One "gencode", "ensembl", "ncbi", "t2t", "mane", "fantom". organism "human" (default) "mouse". Ensembl sets default species (homo_sapiens / mus_musculus). file_type "gff" (default), "gtf", "fasta" (transcript sequences; Ensembl cdna.file), "ncrna_fasta" (Ensembl non-coding transcript sequences), "genome_fasta" (genome sequence; provided MANE) "polya" (GENCODE manually annotated poly() sites signals, polyAs.gff3.gz; see polya_sites()). region Annotation flavour: "" (default; reference chromosomes, patches, haplotypes scaffolds), "chr" (reference chromosomes ) "primary" (primary assembly). file_type = "genome_fasta", "primary" selects primary assembly genome values full patched / toplevel genome. Ignored NCBI MANE. species Ensembl species name lower snake case ("homo_sapiens", "arabidopsis_thaliana"). Defaults organism. division Ensembl division: "vertebrates" (default, main Ensembl site), "plants", "metazoa", "fungi" "protists". accession NCBI assembly accession (GCF_... GCA_...), required reference = "ncbi". mane_source Identifier space MANE files: "ensembl" (default) "refseq". output_path Directory file saved. Defaults ":cache:", package cache (see get_isoformic_cache()). timeout_limit Maximum time seconds download. Takes precedence options("timeout"). title: Frozen Reference Datasets — frozen_data

title: Convert a GFF3/GTF Annotation to Parquet Files — prepare_isoformic_annotation
text: Reading full human GENCODE release (3 million features, gzip-compressed) takes seconds; result cached repeated calls file output location return immediately. parser vocabulary-agnostic annotations different providers assemblies work way: GENCODE GFF3/GTF (GRCh38, GRCm39): gene/transcript/exon features gene_id, transcript_id, gene_type, transcript_type. Ensembl Ensembl Rapid Release GFF3 (e.g. T2T-CHM13 GCA_009914755.4): ncRNA_gene, mRNA, lnc_RNA, ... features, gene:/transcript: prefixed IDs, biotype, rank. NCBI RefSeq GFF3 (e.g. GCF_009914755.1_T2T-CHM13v2.0): gene-/rna- prefixed IDs, gene_biotype, mRNA/lnc_RNA/miRNA features pseudogenes carrying exons directly. T2T consortium Liftoff CAT/Liftoff GFF3 (RefSeq GENCODE lifted CHM13) HPRC per-haplotype CAT annotations: transcript_biotype, gbkey, source_gene / source_transcript attributes, kept source_gene_id / source_transcript_id lifted annotations can mapped back GRCh38 GENCODE RefSeq identifiers. MANE GFF3/GTF CHESS GFF3 (vocabulary GENCODE/RefSeq). FANTOM CAT (FANTOM5 lv1-lv4) FANTOM6 CAT GTF: __na placeholders become NA, geneClass used gene (, transcript type, transcript) type, geneCategory, DHS_type, coding_status, cumulative_support TIEScore kept. CAGE cluster identifiers come FANTOM ID mapping table, see add_fantom_cat_tables(). StringTie, Bambu, FLAIR, IsoQuant SQANTI3 GTF files long-read assembled transcriptomes: reference_id/cmp_ref, ref_gene_id ref_gene_name populate source identifiers gene names; novel transcripts without biotype get transcript_type = NA add_sqanti_classification() assigns SQANTI3 structural categories. Genes features gene-like type parents transcripts; transcripts features transcript-like type parents exons. Transcript types normalised (mRNA protein_coding, lnc_RNA lncRNA) fall back feature type (miRNA, snRNA, ...) biotype attribute exists. genes: gene_id, gene_name, gene_type, source_gene_id, gene_class, gene_category, dhs_type, coding_status, cumulative_support (FANTOM CAT attributes, NA elsewhere), haplotype, seqid, start_pos, end_pos, strand. transcripts: transcript_id, transcript_name, transcript_type, gene_id, source_gene_id, source_transcript_id, tags (comma-separated tag attributes MANE_Select, basic, Ensembl_canonical), is_canonical (TRUE MANE Select, Ensembl canonical RefSeq Select transcripts), coding_status (FANTOM CAT), transcript_support_level (GENCODE TSL), tie_score (FANTOM CAT TIEScore), cds_start, cds_end, cds_length (aggregated CDS features; NA non-coding transcripts), haplotype, seqid, start_pos, end_pos, strand, n_exons, tx_length. exons: exon_id, transcript_id, exon_number, haplotype, seqid, start_pos, end_pos, strand. metadata: key, value (source file, format, header pragmas, creation time). seq_regions: seqid, start_pos, end_pos.

what: Productivity of Transcripts and Genes — productivity
title: Productivity of Transcripts and Genes — productivity
text: biotype split used workflow (protein coding versus retained intron, nonsense-mediated decay, ...) proxy. functions make productivity computed, graded property every transcript summarise per gene: transcript_productivity() classifies assayed transcript "productive" (complete ORF, predicted NMD, ORF canonical isoform), "altered_productive" (complete ORF, NMD, different ORF canonical isoform: alternative start, -frame change, frameshift stop novel sequence), "unproductive" (ORF, premature stop codon 50-nt rule, stop codon, unproductive biotype nonsense_mediated_decay, retained_intron, protein_coding_CDS_not_defined, longest ORF without coding potential), "noncoding" (transcripts genes without coding isoform) "uncertain" (incomplete CDS annotation without premature stop, credible ORF unrelated canonical one, FANTOM uncertain_coding). reason column explains call source tells whether came sequence ("sequence", annotation transcript sequences, see extract_transcript_sequences() transcript_orfs()), annotation ("annotation") external evidence ("evidence"). Evidence columns take precedence, order: productivity_evidence column added add_annotation_columns(), validated NMD exon (add_nmd_exons()), Ribo-seq ORF matching transcript's ORF (add_riboseq_orfs()), APPRIS principal isoform (add_appris()). productive_fraction() share gene's expression carried productive (altered productive) isoforms, per sample per group, difference last first group level. gene whose expression flat productive fraction drops post-transcriptional regulation call gene-level differential expression misses. inferential replicates (inf_reps, Salmon bootstraps Gibbs samples) reports uncertainty fraction, reference (gtex_reference()) difference healthy-tissue baseline. productivity_fractions() splits gene's expression productivity classes , unproductive isoforms, mechanism (nmd, retained_intron, no_orf, non_stop, ). test_productive_fraction() tests change productive fraction two groups counts, quasi-binomial model per gene (pooled proportions per group, Pearson -dispersion, t test log odds ratio, BH adjustment). run_productivity_enrichment() ranks genes change productive fraction two groups runs gene set enrichment (fgsea) gene symbols, captures regulated unproductive splicing (-NMD) directly. poison_exons() lists exons occur unproductive isoforms genes also productive isoforms overlap exon productive isoform (cassette poison / NMD exons, opposed retained introns alternative splice sites); plot_genomic_context() outlines highlight_poison_exons. benchmark_productivity() measures rules annotation biotypes: recall nonsense_mediated_decay retained_intron transcripts sequence/structure rules alone, share protein_coding canonical transcripts called productive. productivity_palette() gives colours classes.

title: Attach External Productivity Evidence to an Annotation — productivity_evidence
text: functions add evidence columns transcript table annotation directory x frozen datasets (frozen_data), transcript_productivity() can use observed translation decay instead rules alone. Identifiers matched without version. add_appris() adds appris_annotation (PRINCIPAL:1 ... ALTERNATIVE:2, MINOR), appris_principal, appris_score method scores (firestar_residues, matador_structure, corsair_conservation, spade_domain_score, thump_tm_helices, trifid_score). Principal isoforms productive evidence. add_riboseq_orfs() adds riboseq_n_orfs (Ribo-seq ORFs compatible transcript's exon structure), riboseq_orf_types, riboseq_main_orf (TRUE translated ORF coincides transcript's ORF, transcript_orfs() sequences available else annotated CDS) riboseq_uorf. translated main ORF productive evidence. Phase 1 ORFs list compatible transcripts; ORFs also matched exon-block compatibility (every block inside exon, consecutive blocks consecutive exons, internal block boundaries exon boundaries). add_nmd_exons() adds nmd_validated_exon, TRUE transcript contains exon exact coordinates NMD-inducing cassette exon validated NMD inhibition (Karousis et al. 2021), one listed NMD isoforms. unproductive evidence. function returns annotation directory path invisibly invalidates object caches x (next call method rereads annotation).

what: Open Reading Frames of Transcripts from Their Sequences — transcript_orfs
title: Open Reading Frames of Transcripts from Their Sequences — transcript_orfs
text: Computes, every assayed transcript, open reading frame (ORF) sequence-level features decide whether productive. Requires transcript sequences annotation directory (see extract_transcript_sequences()). ORF transcript comes first applicable source (orf_source): "annotation": complete annotated CDS. stop codon added annotation excludes (GENCODE ) ORF re-read annotated start codon first -frame stop, CDS match sequence corrected (annotation_cds_agrees = FALSE). Transcripts tagged seleno, ribosomal_slippage non_ATG_start keep annotated CDS. "projected": start codon gene's canonical isoform lies exon transcript reads ATG ; translation proceeds position first -frame stop (ORFanage approach). rescues novel isoforms without CDS. "annotation_partial": annotated CDS flagged incomplete (cds_start_NF / cds_end_NF) whose start projected; annotated span kept, 3' end known NMD rule still applies (GENCODE annotates many NMD transcripts way). "longest": none ; longest ATG--stop ORF least min_orf_length nt used coding_probability tells whether believable. "none": ORF least min_orf_length nt. ORF function derives stop codon (NA translation runs transcript end, non-stop decay substrate), UTR lengths, uORFs 5' UTR (n_uorf, complete upstream ORFs; n_overlapping_uorf, --frame upstream ORFs overlapping main start), genomic coordinates start stop, whether start stop shared canonical isoform whether reading frame stop codon frame canonical ORF (frame_vs_canonical), NMD class: "ptc": stop lies nmd_rule nt upstream last exon-exon junction (50-nt rule), NMD predicted. "ptc_start_proximal": , ORF shorter start_proximal nt; still called unproductive, note transcripts can escape NMD translation re-initiation. "non_stop": -frame stop codon. "long_3utr": premature stop, 3' UTR longer long_utr3 nt (default Inf, flag unless asked ). "none": NMD feature. NA: stop codon transcript whose 3' end annotated incomplete (cds_end_NF / mRNA_end_NF, column end_incomplete), nothing can said. coding_potential() scores every transcript's longest ORF Fickett TESTCODE statistic -frame hexamer usage score, combined logistic model trained GENCODE coding versus lncRNA transcripts (see data-raw/build_coding_model.R); coding_probability coding_cutoff (0.364, CPAT human cutoff) called coding.

what: Read and cut the transcript trees of TreeTerminus — treeterminus
title: Read and cut the transcript trees of TreeTerminus — treeterminus
text: TreeTerminus builds, Salmon replicates, forest transcript trees: leaves transcripts every internal node sum transcripts , built inferential uncertainty falls tree ascended.
